L16: ## 30.18 Chow's Lemma
L17: 
L18: In this section we prove Chow's lemma in the Noetherian case (Lemma 【11†30.18.1】). In Limits, Section 【12†32.12】 we prove some variants for the non-Noetherian case.
L19: 
L20: reference
L21: 
L22: 【11†Lemma 30.18.1.】 Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme. Let $f : X \to S$ be a separated morphism of finite type. Then there exist an $n \geq 0$ and a diagram
L23: 
L24: \[ \xymatrix{ X \ar[rd] & X' \ar[d] \ar[l]^\pi \ar[r] & \mathbf{P}^ n_ S \ar[dl] \\ & S & } \]
L25: where $X' \to \mathbf{P}^ n_ S$ is an immersion, and $\pi : X' \to X$ is proper and surjective. Moreover, we may arrange it such that there exists a dense open subscheme $U \subset X$ such that $\pi ^{-1}(U) \to U$ is an isomorphism.
L26: Proof. All of the schemes we will encounter during the rest of the proof are going to be of finite type over the Noetherian scheme $S$ and hence Noetherian (see Morphisms, Lemma 【13†29.15.6】). All morphisms between them will automatically be quasi-compact, locally of finite type and quasi-separated, see Morphisms, Lemma 【14†29.15.8】 and Properties, Lemmas 【15†28.5.4】 and 【16†28.5.8】.
L27: The scheme $X$ has only finitely many irreducible components (Properties, Lemma 【17†28.5.7】). Say $X = X_1 \cup \ldots \cup X_ r$ is the decomposition of $X$ into irreducible components. Let $\eta _ i \in X_ i$ be the generic point. For every point $x \in X$ there exists an affine open $U_ x \subset X$ which contains $x$ and each of the generic points $\eta _ i$. See Properties, Lemma 【18†28.30.4】.
L28: Since $X$ is quasi-compact, we can find a finite affine open covering $X = U_1 \cup \ldots \cup U_ m$ such that each $U_ i$ contains $\eta _1, \ldots , \eta _ r$. In particular we conclude that the open $U = U_1 \cap \ldots \cap U_ m \subset X$ is a dense open. This and the fact that the $U_ i$ are affine opens covering $X$ are all that we will use below.
L29: Let $X^* \subset X$ be the scheme theoretic closure of $U \to X$, see Morphisms, Definition 【19†29.6.2】. Let $U_ i^* = X^* \cap U_ i$. Note that $U_ i^*$ is a closed subscheme of $U_ i$. Hence $U_ i^*$ is affine. Since $U$ is dense in $X$ the morphism $X^* \to X$ is a surjective closed immersion. It is an isomorphism over $U$. Hence we may replace $X$ by $X^*$ and $U_ i$ by $U_ i^*$ and assume that $U$ is scheme theoretically dense in $X$, see Morphisms, Definition 【20†29.7.1】.
L30: By Morphisms, Lemma 【21†29.40.3】 we can find an immersion $j_ i : U_ i \to \mathbf{P}_ S^{n_ i}$ for each $i$. By Morphisms, Lemma 【22†29.7.7】 we can find closed subschemes $Z_ i \subset \mathbf{P}_ S^{n_ i}$ such that $j_ i : U_ i \to Z_ i$ is a scheme theoretically dense open immersion. Note that $Z_ i \to S$ is proper, see Morphisms, Lemma 【23†29.44.5】. Consider the morphism
L31: \[ j = (j_1|_ U, \ldots , j_ m|_ U) : U \longrightarrow \mathbf{P}_ S^{n_1} \times _ S \ldots \times _ S \mathbf{P}_ S^{n_ m}. \]
L32: 
L33: By the lemma cited above we can find a closed subscheme $Z$ of $\mathbf{P}_ S^{n_1} \times _ S \ldots \times _ S \mathbf{P}_ S^{n_ m}$ such that $j : U \to Z$ is an open immersion and such that $U$ is scheme theoretically dense in $Z$. The morphism $Z \to S$ is proper. Consider the $i$th projection
L34: 
L35: \[ \text{pr}_ i|_ Z : Z \longrightarrow \mathbf{P}^{n_ i}_ S. \]
L36: This morphism factors through $Z_ i$ (see Morphisms, Lemma 【24†29.6.6】). Denote $p_ i : Z \to Z_ i$ the induced morphism. This is a proper morphism, see Morphisms, Lemma 【25†29.42.7】 for example. At this point we have that $U \subset U_ i \subset Z_ i$ are scheme theoretically dense open immersions. Moreover, we can think of $Z$ as the scheme theoretic image of the “diagonal” morphism $U \to Z_1 \times _ S \ldots \times _ S Z_ m$.
L37: Set $V_ i = p_ i^{-1}(U_ i)$. Note that $p_ i|_{V_ i} : V_ i \to U_ i$ is proper. Set $X' = V_1 \cup \ldots \cup V_ m$. By construction $X'$ has an immersion into the scheme $\mathbf{P}^{n_1}_ S \times _ S \ldots \times _ S \mathbf{P}^{n_ m}_ S$. Thus by the Segre embedding (see Constructions, Lemma 【26†27.13.6】) we see that $X'$ has an immersion into a projective space over $S$.
L38: We claim that the morphisms $p_ i|_{V_ i}: V_ i \to U_ i$ glue to a morphism $X' \to X$. Namely, it is clear that $p_ i|_ U$ is the identity map from $U$ to $U$. Since $U \subset X'$ is scheme theoretically dense by construction, it is also scheme theoretically dense in the open subscheme $V_ i \cap V_ j$. Thus we see that $p_ i|_{V_ i \cap V_ j} = p_ j|_{V_ i \cap V_ j}$ as morphisms into the separated $S$-scheme $X$, see Morphisms, Lemma 【27†29.7.10】. We denote the resulting morphism $\pi : X' \to X$.
L39: We claim that $\pi ^{-1}(U_ i) = V_ i$. Since $\pi |_{V_ i} = p_ i|_{V_ i}$ it follows that $V_ i \subset \pi ^{-1}(U_ i)$. Consider the diagram
L40: 
L41: \[ \xymatrix{ V_ i \ar[r] \ar[rd]_{p_ i|_{V_ i}} & \pi ^{-1}(U_ i) \ar[d] \\ & U_ i } \]
L42: 
L43: Since $V_ i \to U_ i$ is proper we see that the image of the horizontal arrow is closed, see Morphisms, Lemma 【25†29.42.7】. Since $V_ i \subset \pi ^{-1}(U_ i)$ is scheme theoretically dense (as it contains $U$) we conclude that $V_ i = \pi ^{-1}(U_ i)$ as claimed.
L44: This shows that $\pi ^{-1}(U_ i) \to U_ i$ is identified with the proper morphism $p_ i|_{V_ i} : V_ i \to U_ i$. Hence we see that $X$ has a finite affine covering $X = \bigcup U_ i$ such that the restriction of $\pi $ is proper on each member of the covering. Thus by Morphisms, Lemma 【28†29.42.3】 we see that $\pi $ is proper.
L45: 
L46: Finally we have to show that $\pi ^{-1}(U) = U$. To see this we argue in the same way as above using the diagram
L47: 
L48: \[ \xymatrix{ U \ar[r] \ar[rd] & \pi ^{-1}(U) \ar[d] \\ & U } \]
L49: and using that $\text{id}_ U : U \to U$ is proper and that $U$ is scheme theoretically dense in $\pi ^{-1}(U)$. $\square$
L50: 
L51: 【29†Remark 30.18.2.】 In the situation of Chow's Lemma 【11†30.18.1】:
L52: 
L53:   1. The morphism $\pi $ is actually H-projective (hence projective, see Morphisms, Lemma 【30†29.44.3】) since the morphism $X' \to \mathbf{P}^ n_ S \times _ S X = \mathbf{P}^ n_ X$ is a closed immersion (use the fact that $\pi $ is proper, see Morphisms, Lemma 【25†29.42.7】).
L54:   2. We may assume that $\pi ^{-1}(U)$ is scheme theoretically dense in $X'$. Namely, we can simply replace $X'$ by the scheme theoretic closure of $\pi ^{-1}(U)$. In this case we can think of $U$ as a scheme theoretically dense open subscheme of $X'$. See Morphisms, Section 【31†29.6】.
L55: 
L56:   3. If $X$ is reduced then we may choose $X'$ reduced. This is clear from (2).

L16: > Abstract:We prove that any noetherian quasi-excellent scheme of characteristic zero admits a strong desingularization which is functorial with respect to all regular morphisms. We show that as an easy formal consequence of this result one obtains strong functorial desingularization for many other spaces of characteristic zero including quasi-excellent stacks and formal schemes, and complex and non-archimedean analytic spaces.
L17: Moreover, these functors easily generalize to non-compact setting by use of converging blow up hyper-sequences with regular centers.

L16: ## 31.33 Blowing up
L17: 
L18: Blowing up is an important tool in algebraic geometry.
L19: 
L20: 【11†Definition 31.33.1.】 Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_ X$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, and let $Z \subset X$ be the closed subscheme corresponding to $\mathcal{I}$, see Schemes, Definition 【12†26.10.2】. The blowing up of $X$ along $Z$, or the blowing up of $X$ in the ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}$ is the morphism
L21: \[ b : \underline{\text{Proj}}_ X \left(\bigoplus \nolimits _{n \geq 0} \mathcal{I}^ n\right) \longrightarrow X \]
L22: 
L23: The exceptional divisor of the blowup is the inverse image $b^{-1}(Z)$. Sometimes $Z$ is called the center of the blowup.
L24: 
L25: We will see later that the exceptional divisor is an effective Cartier divisor. Moreover, the blowing up is characterized as the “smallest” scheme over $X$ such that the inverse image of $Z$ is an effective Cartier divisor.
L26: If $b : X' \to X$ is the blowup of $X$ in $Z$, then we often denote $\mathcal{O}_{X'}(n)$ the twists of the structure sheaf. Note that these are invertible $\mathcal{O}_{X'}$-modules and that $\mathcal{O}_{X'}(n) = \mathcal{O}_{X'}(1)^{\otimes n}$ because $X'$ is the relative Proj of a quasi-coherent graded $\mathcal{O}_ X$-algebra which is generated in degree $1$, see Constructions, Lemma 【13†27.16.11】.
L27: Note that $\mathcal{O}_{X'}(1)$ is $b$-relatively very ample, even though $b$ need not be of finite type or even quasi-compact, because $X'$ comes equipped with a closed immersion into $\mathbf{P}(\mathcal{I})$, see Morphisms, Example 【14†29.39.3】.
L28: 【15†Lemma 31.33.2.】 Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{I} \subset \mathcal{O}_ X$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. Let $U = \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A)$ be an affine open subscheme of $X$ and let $I \subset A$ be the ideal corresponding to $\mathcal{I}|_ U$. If $b : X' \to X$ is the blowup of $X$ in $\mathcal{I}$, then there is a canonical isomorphism
L29: 
L30: \[ b^{-1}(U) = \text{Proj}(\bigoplus \nolimits _{d \geq 0} I^ d) \]
L31: of $b^{-1}(U)$ with the homogeneous spectrum of the Rees algebra of $I$ in $A$. Moreover, $b^{-1}(U)$ has an affine open covering by spectra of the affine blowup algebras $A[\frac{I}{a}]$.
L32: Proof. The first statement is clear from the construction of the relative Proj via glueing, see Constructions, Section 【16†27.15】. For $a \in I$ denote $a^{(1)}$ the element $a$ seen as an element of degree $1$ in the Rees algebra $\bigoplus _{n \geq 0} I^ n$. Since these elements generate the Rees algebra over $A$ we see that $\text{Proj}(\bigoplus _{d \geq 0} I^ d)$ is covered by the affine opens $D_{+}(a^{(1)})$.
L33: The affine scheme $D_{+}(a^{(1)})$ is the spectrum of the affine blowup algebra $A' = A[\frac{I}{a}]$, see Algebra, Definition 【17†10.70.1】. This finishes the proof. $\square$
L34: slogan
L35: 
L36: 【18†Lemma 31.33.3.】 Let $X_1 \to X_2$ be a flat morphism of schemes. Let $Z_2 \subset X_2$ be a closed subscheme. Let $Z_1$ be the inverse image of $Z_2$ in $X_1$. Let $X'_ i$ be the blowup of $Z_ i$ in $X_ i$. Then there exists a cartesian diagram
L37: 
L38: \[ \xymatrix{ X_1' \ar[r] \ar[d] & X_2' \ar[d] \\ X_1 \ar[r] & X_2 } \]
L39: 
L40: of schemes.
L41: Proof. Let $\mathcal{I}_2$ be the ideal sheaf of $Z_2$ in $X_2$. Denote $g : X_1 \to X_2$ the given morphism. Then the ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}_1$ of $Z_1$ is the image of $g^*\mathcal{I}_2 \to \mathcal{O}_{X_1}$ (by definition of the inverse image, see Schemes, Definition 【19†26.17.7】). By Constructions, Lemma 【20†27.16.10】 we see that $X_1 \times _{X_2} X_2'$ is the relative Proj of $\bigoplus _{n \geq 0} g^*\mathcal{I}_2^ n$.
L42: Because $g$ is flat the map $g^*\mathcal{I}_2^ n \to \mathcal{O}_{X_1}$ is injective with image $\mathcal{I}_1^ n$. Thus we see that $X_1 \times _{X_2} X_2' = X_1'$. $\square$
L43: 【21†Lemma 31.33.4.】 Let $X$ be a scheme. Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subscheme. The blowing up $b : X' \to X$ of $Z$ in $X$ has the following properties:
L44: 
L45:   1. $b|_{b^{-1}(X \setminus Z)} : b^{-1}(X \setminus Z) \to X \setminus Z$ is an isomorphism,
L46: 
L47:   2. the exceptional divisor $E = b^{-1}(Z)$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $X'$,
L48: 
L49:   3. there is a canonical isomorphism $\mathcal{O}_{X'}(-1) = \mathcal{O}_{X'}(E)$
L50: Proof. As blowing up commutes with restrictions to open subschemes (Lemma 【18†31.33.3】) the first statement just means that $X' = X$ if $Z = \emptyset $. In this case we are blowing up in the ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I} = \mathcal{O}_ X$ and the result follows from Constructions, Example 【22†27.8.14】.
L51: The second statement is local on $X$, hence we may assume $X$ affine. Say $X = \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A)$ and $Z = \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A/I)$. By Lemma 【15†31.33.2】 we see that $X'$ is covered by the spectra of the affine blowup algebras $A' = A[\frac{I}{a}]$. Then $IA' = aA'$ and $a$ maps to a nonzerodivisor in $A'$ according to Algebra, Lemma 【23†10.70.2】.
L52: This proves the lemma as the inverse image of $Z$ in $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A')$ corresponds to $\mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A'/IA') \subset \mathop{\mathrm{Spec}}(A')$.
L53: Consider the canonical map $\psi _{univ, 1} : b^*\mathcal{I} \to \mathcal{O}_{X'}(1)$, see discussion following Constructions, Definition 【24†27.16.7】. We claim that this factors through an isomorphism $\mathcal{I}_ E \to \mathcal{O}_{X'}(1)$ (which proves the final assertion). Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the full subcategory of $(\mathit{Sch}/X)$ consisting of $Y \to X$ such that the inverse image of $Z$ is an effective Cartier divisor on $Y$.
